scenario: 面试题:给 20 亿用户做视频推荐,端到端延迟预算 sub-200ms,目录里有十亿量级候选视频。
scenario_en: Interview prompt: video recs for 2B users with a sub-200ms budget and a billion-scale candidate catalog.
q: 为什么几乎所有大厂推荐/搜索都用「检索+排序」两阶段级联,而不是一个模型打分到底？
q_en: Why do MAANG rec/search stacks use a retrieval-then-ranking cascade instead of one model scoring everything?
why: 检索(retrieval)用轻量方法把十亿候选快速收到数百个;排序(ranking)再用表达力强的重模型给这数百个精打分重排。一个重模型给十亿候选逐个打分在 sub-200ms 内不可能,分两阶段是为在延迟预算内兼顾规模与精度。
why_en: Retrieval narrows billions to hundreds cheaply, then ranking rescoring the hundreds with an expressive model, because one heavy model over billions can't fit sub-200ms.
diagram:
flowchart LR C["十亿候选"] --> R["检索
轻量, 两塔+ANN"] R --> H["数百候选"] H --> K["排序
W&D/DCN 精打分"] K --> T["最终数十条"]
options: 用单个表达力强的重模型直接给全部十亿候选逐个打分,再取分最高的数十条返回给用户
检索轻量地把十亿候选收到数百,排序再用重模型精打分
先用重排序模型给十亿候选全部精排,再从排好序的结果里随机采样出数百个做检索
只用一层基于关键词匹配的规则过滤,完全不训练任何模型,靠人工配规则覆盖十亿候选
options_en: Use one expressive heavy model to score all billion candidates one by one, then return the top few dozen.
Retrieval cheaply narrows billions to hundreds, then ranking rescores those hundreds precisely.
Fully rank all billion candidates with the heavy model first, then randomly sample hundreds as the retrieval step.
Use only one layer of keyword-match rules with no trained model, hand-configuring rules to cover a billion candidates.
optionExplanations: 重模型给十亿候选逐个打分远超 sub-200ms 预算,单阶段在规模上根本跑不完。
对;轻量检索先收窄、重排序再精打分,正是延迟预算下兼顾规模与精度的标准级联。
顺序颠倒:排序是给少量候选精打分的,不可能先精排十亿再采样,那样毫无意义还更慢。
纯关键词规则无法个性化,也捕捉不到语义相似,扛不住规模与质量要求。
optionExplanations_en: A heavy model scoring a billion one by one far exceeds sub-200ms; a single stage can't finish at scale.
Correct — light retrieval narrows first and heavy ranking scores precisely, the standard cascade under a latency budget.
Order reversed: ranking scores a small set, so fully ranking a billion then sampling is pointless and slower.
Pure keyword rules can't personalize or capture semantic similarity and can't meet scale and quality needs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 级联第一阶段,用轻量方法从海量目录快速筛出数百候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Retrieval is the first cascade stage, cheaply narrowing a huge catalog to a few hundred candidates.

termDefinitions.meaning: 级联第二阶段,用表达力强的重模型给候选集精细打分重排。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Ranking is the second cascade stage, scoring the candidate set finely with an expressive model.

termDefinitions.meaning: 指头部大型科技公司,其推荐/搜索普遍采用两阶段级联。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MAANG refers to big-tech companies whose rec/search stacks commonly use a two-stage cascade.

scenario: 要从十亿量级物料里做候选检索,团队原本用 GBDT 打分,发现它靠手工特征、也没有稠密语义表示,召回上不去。
scenario_en: Retrieving candidates from a billion-scale corpus, the team's GBDT relies on hand-crafted features and lacks dense semantic reps, so recall stalls.
q: 为什么 LR/GBDT 这类强表格基线在十亿级检索这一步会撞天花板？
q_en: Why do strong tabular baselines like LR/GBDT hit a ceiling at billion-scale retrieval?
why: LR/GBDT 依赖手工交叉特征、没有可比对的稠密语义 embedding,无法把物料压成向量做近邻检索,只能逐条打分,十亿量级下召回和延迟都撑不住。检索这步需要的是稠密向量+ANN,正是两塔模型的强项。
why_en: LR/GBDT lean on hand-crafted features with no dense semantic embeddings to index for nearest-neighbor search, so they can't scale retrieval to billions.
tradeoff: 两塔稠密向量+ANN(可近邻检索十亿) vs LR/GBDT 手工特征(表格强但无语义向量、检索撞墙)
options: 因为 LR/GBDT 训练太慢,换成两塔只是为了缩短训练时间,和检索机制本身没关系
因为 LR/GBDT 靠手工特征、没有稠密语义向量,做不了 ANN 检索
因为 LR/GBDT 精度天生比神经网络低,在任何排序任务上都该被淘汰替换掉
因为 LR/GBDT 只能处理图像输入,面对视频这种非结构化数据完全无法建模
options_en: Because LR/GBDT train too slowly; switching to two-tower just shortens training time, unrelated to retrieval itself.
Because LR/GBDT rely on hand-crafted features with no dense semantic vectors, so ANN retrieval is impossible.
Because LR/GBDT are inherently less accurate than neural nets and should be replaced on every ranking task.
Because LR/GBDT only handle image inputs and cannot model unstructured data like video at all.
whenOtherWins: 若候选集本就只有几千条(小目录),不需要 ANN 近邻检索,GBDT 直接逐条打分反而简单够用,不必上两塔。
whenOtherWins_en: If the candidate set is only a few thousand items, no ANN retrieval is needed and GBDT scoring each is simpler and sufficient.
optionExplanations: 问题不是训练速度,而是 GBDT 产不出可做近邻检索的稠密语义向量,换两塔是为了检索机制而非训练提速。
对;检索需要稠密 embedding + ANN,GBDT 的手工特征范式压不出可比对向量,十亿级就撞墙。
GBDT 在表格排序上仍很强,并非处处该淘汰;它的短板只在「大规模语义检索」这一步。
GBDT 恰恰擅长结构化表格特征,说它只能处理图像是完全弄反了。
optionExplanations_en: The issue isn't training speed but that GBDT can't produce dense semantic vectors for nearest-neighbor search; two-tower is about the retrieval mechanism.
Correct — retrieval needs dense embeddings plus ANN, and GBDT's hand-crafted paradigm can't yield comparable vectors, so it hits a wall at billions.
GBDT remains strong on tabular ranking and isn't obsolete everywhere; its weakness is only large-scale semantic retrieval.
GBDT actually excels at structured tabular features; saying it only handles images is exactly backwards.

termDefinitions.meaning: 梯度提升决策树,强表格基线,靠手工特征,但产不出稠密语义向量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GBDT (Gradient-Boosted Decision Trees) is a strong tabular baseline using hand-crafted features but yields no dense semantic vectors.

termDefinitions.meaning: 逻辑回归,线性基线模型,大致相当于 Wide & Deep 的 wide 部分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LR (Logistic Regression) is a linear baseline, roughly the wide component of Wide & Deep.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把物料/用户映射成的低维稠密向量,可做点积相似度与近邻检索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding is a low-dimensional dense vector for an item/user, enabling dot-product similarity and nearest-neighbor search.

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻检索,在向量空间快速找 top-K 相似项,如 FAISS/ScaNN。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) search quickly finds top-K similar vectors, e.g. FAISS/ScaNN.

scenario: 面试官让你在白板上画出用于检索的两塔(dual/bi-encoder)模型结构。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to sketch the two-tower (dual/bi-encoder) model used for retrieval.
q: 两塔模型的结构是什么,两座塔各吃什么、各吐什么？
q_en: What is the two-tower structure — what does each tower take in and put out?
why: 两座独立网络:用户塔编码用户侧信号、物品塔编码物品侧信号,各输出同维稠密向量;训练时最大化正样本对的点积/余弦相似度、把负样本推远。同维才能做相似度比对。
why_en: Two separate nets — a user tower and item tower — each output a same-dimension dense vector, trained to maximize dot-product/cosine similarity on positive pairs.
diagram:
flowchart TD U["用户塔
观看史/人口/上下文"] --> UV["用户向量"] I["物品塔
ID/标题/类别/热度"] --> IV["物品向量"] UV --> D(("点积/余弦相似度")) IV --> D
options: 一座塔把用户和物品特征拼接后一起输入,只输出一个联合匹配分,产不出可离线索引的向量
用户塔、物品塔两座独立网络各输出同维稠密向量,训练最大化正样本对相似度、推远负样本
物品塔省去独立编码,把物品原始类别 ID 直接当向量,靠 ID 是否相同打分
两座塔共享全部参数、只训练出一个向量,再拿同一个向量既当用户表示又当物品表示
options_en: One tower concatenates user and item features and outputs a single joint match score, producing no offline-indexable vector.
A user tower and item tower are two separate nets each outputting a same-dim dense vector, trained to maximize positive-pair similarity and push negatives apart.
The item tower skips its own encoding and uses the item's raw category ID directly as the vector, scoring by whether the IDs match.
The two towers share all parameters and train only one vector, using that same vector to represent both the user and the item at once.
optionExplanations: 拼接后只出一个联合匹配分正是 cross-encoder 的做法,它产不出可离线索引的物品向量,不是两塔。
对;两塔各自编码、输出同维向量,训练拉近正样本对、推远负样本,才能后续做点积检索。
把类别 ID 直接当向量等于精确匹配,ID 不同就打不上分,学不到语义相近物品之间的相似度,失去两塔的意义。
两塔通常不共享参数;若强行共享成一个向量,就分不出谁是用户谁是物品,embedding 空间会退化、召回下降。
optionExplanations_en: Concatenate-then-score is the cross-encoder approach, which yields no offline-indexable item vector and isn't two-tower.
Correct — each tower encodes separately into same-dim vectors, trained to pull positive pairs together and push negatives apart for later dot-product retrieval.
Using the raw category ID as the vector is exact matching — items with different IDs never score, so semantically similar-but-different items are never learned, defeating the point of two-tower.
The towers usually don't share parameters; forcing them into one shared vector loses the ability to tell user from item, and the embedding space degrades along with recall.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户塔与物品塔两座独立网络,各输出同维稠密向量做相似度检索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-tower (dual/bi-encoder) uses separate user and item nets, each output a same-dim vector for similarity retrieval.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个输出与全部输入相连的神经网络层,两塔各叠 2-3 层压出向量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fully-connected (FC) layer connects every output to all inputs; each tower stacks 2-3 to produce its vector.

scenario: 十亿量级物品、每次用户请求要在 sub-10ms 内取回 top-K 候选,不能在请求时给十亿物品逐个跑神经网络。
scenario_en: Billions of items, top-K needed in sub-10ms per request; you can't run a net over billions of items at query time.
q: 两塔模型「解耦」这个关键优势具体怎么落到部署上、如何做到 sub-10ms？
q_en: How does the two-tower decoupling advantage translate to deployment and sub-10ms?
why: 物品塔与用户塔解耦:物品 embedding 可离线预计算并灌进 ANN 索引(FAISS/ScaNN),线上只跑用户塔算一个用户向量,再用它到 ANN 里近邻检索 top-K,sub-10ms 完成。省掉了在请求时对十亿物品逐个前向。
why_en: Item embeddings are precomputed offline and indexed in an ANN system; online only the user tower runs, then an ANN top-K lookup returns candidates in sub-10ms.
tradeoff: 两塔解耦(物品离线预算+ANN,只在线跑用户塔,sub-10ms) vs cross-encoder(联合打分、物品无法预算、十亿级不可行)
options: 物品向量离线预算灌进 ANN 索引,线上只跑用户塔再近邻检索 top-K
线上对全部十亿物品逐个跑物品塔,实时算出向量后再和用户向量逐个点积,靠加机器压到 sub-10ms
把用户塔也离线预计算成固定向量,线上不跑任何网络,直接返回昨天缓存好的固定 top-K 列表
线上同时实时跑用户塔和物品塔,把两塔的输出拼接后过一个大网络给每个物品输出联合分数
options_en: Item vectors are precomputed offline into an ANN index; online only the user tower runs, then a top-K nearest-neighbor lookup.
Online run the item tower over all billion items to compute vectors live, then dot-product each against the user vector, brute-forcing sub-10ms with more machines.
Precompute the user tower into a fixed vector too, run no network online, and just return yesterday's cached fixed top-K list.
Online run both towers live, concatenate their outputs, and pass through one big net to emit a joint score per item.
whenOtherWins: 若物品集很小(几千条)且特征频繁变动,离线预计算+ANN 的收益不大,可考虑请求时直接算,甚至用 cross-encoder 追求更高精度。
whenOtherWins_en: If the item set is small and features change often, offline precompute + ANN buys little, so request-time scoring or even a cross-encoder for precision may fit.
optionExplanations: 对;解耦让物品侧离线固化进 ANN,在线只算用户向量再近邻检索,这正是 sub-10ms 的来源。
在请求时对十亿物品逐个前向永远压不进 sub-10ms,加机器也扛不住,这正是解耦要避免的。
缓存固定 top-K 无法个性化、也无法反映用户当前上下文,把在线检索退化成了静态列表。
在线拼接联合打分是 cross-encoder,物品无法预计算,十亿级不可行,与解耦优势背道而驰。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — decoupling freezes the item side into an ANN offline, computing only the user vector online then a nearest-neighbor lookup, the source of sub-10ms.
Forward-passing a billion items per request can never fit sub-10ms and doesn't scale with machines — exactly what decoupling avoids.
A fixed cached top-K can't personalize or reflect current context, degrading online retrieval into a static list.
Live concatenate-and-score is a cross-encoder; items can't be precomputed and billions are infeasible, opposing the decoupling advantage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个主流 ANN 库,把物品向量建索引,支持毫秒级 top-K 近邻检索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FAISS and ScaNN are popular ANN libraries that index item vectors for millisecond top-K nearest-neighbor search.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两塔各自独立编码,物品侧可离线预计算、在线只算用户侧,是两塔的核心部署优势。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Decoupling lets each tower encode independently so items are precomputed offline and only the user side runs online — the key deployment advantage.

scenario: 在检索阶段要在「两塔(bi-encoder)」和「cross-encoder 联合打分」之间取舍。
scenario_en: At the retrieval stage, choosing between a two-tower (bi-encoder) and a cross-encoder that scores jointly.
q: 两塔(bi-encoder)与 cross-encoder 的核心取舍在哪条轴上？
q_en: On what axis do bi-encoder and cross-encoder fundamentally trade off?
why: 取舍是「可预计算/速度 vs 交互建模精度」:两塔分开编码,物品可离线预算+ANN,快但用户-物品交互只靠最后点积,较弱;cross-encoder 把用户物品特征拼在一起联合建模,交互更丰富但每对都要现算、物品无法预计算,十亿级不可行。
why_en: The tradeoff is precomputability/speed vs interaction modeling: bi-encoder precomputes items for fast ANN with weak late interaction, while cross-encoder models rich interaction but can't precompute.
tradeoff: 两塔(可预计算、快、交互弱) vs cross-encoder(交互强、精度高、无法预计算、不可规模化)
options: 两者完全等价,只是名字不同,选哪个都不影响线上速度或离线精度
取舍轴是「可预计算速度 vs 交互建模精度」,两塔快但交互弱
cross-encoder 更快更省,因为它只需要一次前向就能给十亿物品同时打分
两塔精度一定高于 cross-encoder,因为它用了两个网络而不是一个
options_en: They are equivalent and differ only in name, affecting neither online speed nor offline accuracy.
The axis is precomputability/speed vs interaction modeling: two-tower is fast but weak on interaction.
Cross-encoder is faster and cheaper because one forward pass scores all billion items at once.
Two-tower is always more accurate than cross-encoder because it uses two networks instead of one.
optionExplanations: 两者在交互建模和可预计算性上根本不同,直接决定速度与规模,绝非等价。
对;这条轴决定了两塔用于十亿级检索、cross-encoder 只能用于少量候选的精排。
说反了:cross-encoder 每对都要现算,无法一次前向给十亿物品打分,慢且不可规模化。
网络数量多不等于精度高;交叉编码器的联合交互建模通常在精度上更强,只是没法规模化。
optionExplanations_en: They differ fundamentally on interaction modeling and precomputability, which set speed and scale, so not equivalent.
Correct — this axis is why two-tower serves billion-scale retrieval while cross-encoder only reranks a few candidates.
Backwards: a cross-encoder recomputes per pair and can't score a billion in one pass, so it's slow and unscalable.
More networks doesn't mean higher accuracy; a cross-encoder's joint interaction is usually stronger but unscalable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户与物品特征拼接进一个网络联合打分,交互强但物品无法预计算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-encoder concatenates user and item features into one net for a joint score — rich interaction but no precomputable items.

termDefinitions.meaning: 即两塔,用户与物品各自独立编码成向量,末端做点积相似度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bi-encoder is the two-tower design where user and item are encoded independently, meeting only at a final dot product.

scenario: cross-encoder 精度更高但在十亿级检索上不可行,团队又想在两塔里尽量保住那份精度。
scenario_en: A cross-encoder is more accurate but infeasible for billion-scale retrieval, yet the team wants to keep some of that accuracy in the two-tower.
q: 既然 cross-encoder 精度高却无法规模化,怎么把它的质量迁到可部署的两塔上？
q_en: Since a cross-encoder is accurate but unscalable, how do you transfer its quality into a deployable two-tower?
why: 用知识蒸馏:cross-encoder 当 teacher 出软标签,两塔 student 去拟合。这样两塔保住「物品可预计算+ANN」的部署优势,又吸收 cross-encoder 的交互质量;代价是要额外训练维护 teacher。
why_en: Use knowledge distillation: train an accurate cross-encoder teacher, then fit the two-tower student to the teacher's scores so the student keeps deployability while gaining quality.
options: 把 cross-encoder 的参数直接复制进两塔,让两塔逐层照搬 teacher 的权重就能获得同样精度
放弃两塔,直接线上部署 cross-encoder,靠更强的 GPU 硬扛十亿级逐对打分的延迟
用知识蒸馏:cross-encoder 当 teacher 出软标签,两塔 student 去拟合
只在离线评估时用 cross-encoder,线上两塔完全不受它影响,两者互不关联各训各的
options_en: Copy the cross-encoder's parameters straight into the two-tower, layer by layer, to get the same accuracy.
Drop the two-tower and deploy the cross-encoder online, brute-forcing billion-scale pairwise scoring latency with stronger GPUs.
Use knowledge distillation: the cross-encoder teacher emits soft labels and the two-tower student fits them.
Use the cross-encoder only in offline evaluation; the online two-tower is unaffected and the two are trained independently.
optionExplanations: 两塔与 cross-encoder 结构不同,权重无法逐层照搬;迁移质量靠的是蒸软标签而不是复制参数。
线上直接跑 cross-encoder 逐对打分十亿级不可行,加 GPU 也压不进延迟预算,这正是要绕开的。
对;蒸馏让高精度 teacher 的软标签指导 student,两塔既保住可预计算部署又拿到交互质量。
只离线用等于没把质量迁到线上;蒸馏的意义正是让线上 student 学到 teacher 的判别力。
optionExplanations_en: The two architectures differ, so weights can't be copied layer by layer; quality transfers via distilling soft labels, not copying parameters.
Running a cross-encoder online pairwise at billions is infeasible and GPUs can't fix the budget — exactly what to avoid.
Correct — distillation lets the accurate teacher's soft labels guide the student, so the two-tower keeps deployability and gains interaction quality.
Using it only offline transfers nothing online; distillation exists precisely so the online student learns the teacher's discrimination.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用高精度 teacher 模型的软标签训练更小/更快的 student,迁移其质量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Knowledge distillation trains a smaller/faster student on a high-accuracy teacher's soft labels to transfer its quality.

termDefinitions.meaning: teacher 输出的连续分数或概率分布,比硬标签含更多排序信息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Soft labels are the teacher's continuous scores or probability distribution, carrying more ranking signal than hard labels.

scenario: 训练两塔:要让「用户真正看过的物品」在向量空间里靠近用户向量,其他物品被推远。
scenario_en: Training a two-tower so items a user actually watched sit close to the user vector while others are pushed away.
q: 两塔通常用什么损失/负采样方式训练？
q_en: What loss / negative-sampling scheme typically trains a two-tower?
why: 常用 sampled softmax 或 in-batch negatives:拉近正样本对相似度,把同 batch 其他物品当负样本推远。无需枚举全库负例,batch 内对比就能高效学出可检索 embedding。
why_en: Typically sampled softmax or in-batch negatives: maximize positive-pair similarity while treating other items in the batch as negatives to push apart.
options: 用均方误差回归物品原始像素值,让用户向量逐像素还原出他接下来会点开的那一帧视频画面
用 sampled softmax / in-batch negatives 做批内对比
用监督分类交叉熵直接预测每个物品属于哪个类别标签,完全不涉及用户与物品之间的相似度信号
枚举全库每个物品都当负例逐一对比、不做任何采样,靠遍历十亿量级负例来做精确的对比训练
options_en: Mean-squared error regressing raw item pixels so the user vector reconstructs, pixel by pixel, the video frame they will click next.
Use sampled softmax or in-batch negatives, contrasting within the batch.
Supervised cross-entropy predicting which category label each item belongs to, with no user-item similarity signal involved at all.
Enumerate every item in the corpus as a negative one by one with no sampling, training exactly by iterating billions of negatives.
optionExplanations: 两塔学的是相似度而非像素重建;回归像素既无检索意义也训不出可比对向量。
对;这两种批内负采样用 batch 内对比高效学相似度,是两塔检索的标准训法。
只预测类别标签学不到「用户偏好某物品」的相似度信号,与检索目标不符。
枚举全库十亿负例计算不可行;采样负例正是为了在可承受成本内近似全库对比。
optionExplanations_en: Two-tower learns similarity, not pixel reconstruction; regressing pixels has no retrieval meaning and yields no comparable vectors.
Correct — sampled softmax / in-batch negatives learn similarity efficiently via in-batch contrast, the standard two-tower recipe.
Predicting only category labels learns no user-preference similarity signal, mismatching the retrieval goal.
Enumerating a billion negatives is infeasible; sampling approximates full-corpus contrast at affordable cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把同一 batch 里其他样本的物品当作当前用户的负例,省去全库枚举。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In-batch negatives treat other items in the same batch as negatives for the current user, avoiding full-corpus enumeration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只在采样出的负例子集上算 softmax,近似全库归一化,降低训练成本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sampled softmax computes softmax over a sampled subset of negatives, approximating full normalization at lower cost.

scenario: 两塔只用随机负样本训练,上线后发现召回里混进大量「看似相关其实不相关」的物品,recall 明显下降。
scenario_en: Trained with only random negatives, the two-tower retrieves many 'looks-relevant-but-isn't' items and recall drops noticeably.
q: 只用随机负样本会引发什么问题,怎么修？
q_en: What goes wrong with only random negatives, and how do you fix it?
why: 随机负样本太易,模型只会分「明显无关」、学不会「相似但不相关」的难例 → embedding 退化、recall 降。修法是 hard negative mining:挑相似但不相关的物品当负例逼出更细边界;代价是挖掘有成本。
why_en: Random negatives are mostly obviously irrelevant, so the model only separates the easy cases and recall degrades; hard-negative mining adds similar-but-irrelevant items to sharpen the boundary.
options: 随机负样本会让模型过拟合正样本,修法是把学习率调到极小、训练更久让它慢慢收敛
只能分明显无关、学不会相似但不相关的难例→recall 降;修法 hard negative mining
随机负样本导致向量维度太高,修法是把 embedding 维度砍到个位数以减少噪声
随机负样本本身没有任何问题,recall 下降只可能是 ANN 索引的召回参数没调好,与负采样策略无关
options_en: Random negatives overfit the positives; fix by shrinking the learning rate and training longer to converge slowly.
It only separates obviously irrelevant items and misses hard cases, so recall drops; fix with hard-negative mining.
Random negatives make the vector dimension too high; fix by cutting embedding dim to single digits to reduce noise.
Random negatives cause no problem at all; the recall drop can only be an untuned ANN index recall parameter, unrelated to the negative-sampling strategy.
optionExplanations: 问题不是过拟合正样本,而是负例太易学不到细边界;调学习率救不了负采样的信息缺口。
对;走完「随机负太易→只会分明显无关→难例分不开→recall 降→挖难负例修」整链,是标准诊断与修法。
维度不是根因,盲目砍到个位数反而损失表达力;问题出在负样本难度不够。
recall 下降可直接归因于负采样太易,把它全推给 ANN 参数是误诊。
optionExplanations_en: The issue isn't overfitting positives but negatives too easy to learn a fine boundary; tuning the LR won't fill the sampling gap.
Correct — it walks the chain random-too-easy → only separates obvious → can't split hard cases → recall drops → mine hard negatives, the standard fix.
Dimension isn't the cause; blindly cutting to single digits loses expressiveness — the problem is insufficient negative difficulty.
The recall drop traces directly to too-easy negatives; blaming it entirely on ANN params is a misdiagnosis.

termDefinitions.term: hard negative mining / 难负例挖掘
termDefinitions.meaning: 选相似但不相关的物品当负例,逼模型学出更细的相关性边界。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hard-negative mining picks similar-but-irrelevant items as negatives to force a finer relevance boundary.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检索阶段真正相关物品被取回的比例,是检索质量的核心指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall is the fraction of truly relevant items retrieved, the core retrieval-quality metric.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户/物品映射成的低维稠密向量,用于相似度与近邻检索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding is a low-dimensional dense vector for a user/item, used for similarity and nearest-neighbor search.

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻检索,在向量空间快速找 top-K,负样本太易会拉低其召回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) search finds top-K similar vectors fast; easy negatives lower its recall.

scenario: 端到端 sub-200ms 的推荐里,要给检索和排序分配各自的延迟预算。
scenario_en: In a sub-200ms recommender, you must split the latency budget between retrieval and ranking.
q: 检索与排序阶段各自大致的延迟预算是多少,为什么这么分？
q_en: What are the rough latency budgets for retrieval vs ranking, and why split that way?
why: 检索约 sub-10ms(只跑用户塔 + ANN 近邻),排序约 <50ms(给数百候选跑重模型)。检索面对十亿量级必须极快,所以用可预计算+ANN;排序候选只剩数百、可以付更重的计算换精度。两段之和要卡在端到端预算内。
why_en: Retrieval is about sub-10ms (user tower + ANN) and ranking under 50ms for hundreds of candidates, because retrieval faces billions and must be fastest while ranking can spend more on far fewer items.
options: 检索约 <50ms、排序约 sub-10ms,因为检索要跑重模型、排序只是简单排序
检索约 sub-10ms(用户塔+ANN)、排序约 <50ms(数百候选跑重模型)
检索和排序各分 100ms,平均对半分才公平,和候选量级无关
两阶段都必须在 1ms 内完成,否则系统一定超时无法上线
options_en: Retrieval ~<50ms and ranking ~sub-10ms, because retrieval runs the heavy model and ranking just sorts.
Retrieval ~sub-10ms (user tower + ANN) and ranking ~<50ms (heavy model over hundreds of candidates).
Split 100ms each — an even half-and-half is fair regardless of candidate scale.
Both stages must finish within 1ms or the system will always time out and can't launch.
optionExplanations: 分反了:检索面对十亿必须最快(sub-10ms),排序候选少才付得起更重的计算(<50ms)。
对;检索快(十亿量级)、排序重(数百量级),预算按候选量级与模型重量分配,和内卡在总预算。
对半平均分忽略了候选量级差异:检索面对的规模大得多,必须分到更紧的时间做最轻的活。
1ms 内做完既不必要也不现实;端到端 sub-200ms 才是约束,阶段预算按需分配即可。
optionExplanations_en: Reversed: retrieval faces billions and must be fastest (sub-10ms), while ranking with fewer candidates can afford more compute (<50ms).
Correct — retrieval fast (billions), ranking heavier (hundreds); budget follows candidate scale and model weight, summing within the total.
An even split ignores scale: retrieval faces far more items and must do the lightest work in the tightest time.
Sub-1ms is neither needed nor realistic; the constraint is end-to-end sub-200ms, allocated per stage as needed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分给某阶段的时间上限,各阶段之和不能超过端到端目标(如 sub-200ms)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A latency budget is the time ceiling for a stage; stages must sum within the end-to-end target like sub-200ms.

scenario: 面试官让你画排序用的 Wide & Deep(Google 2016, Google Play)结构。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to sketch Wide & Deep (Google 2016, Google Play) used for ranking.
q: Wide & Deep 的两个组件各做什么,怎么合成 CTR 预测？
q_en: What do Wide & Deep's two components do, and how do they combine for a CTR prediction?
why: Wide 是对稀疏人工交叉特征的线性模型,负责记忆历史高频共现;Deep 是对稠密 embedding 的前馈网,负责泛化到未见组合。两者联合训练、输出相加过 sigmoid 得 CTR。
why_en: Wide is a linear model over sparse manually-crossed features for memorization; Deep is a feed-forward net over dense embeddings for generalization; their outputs sum into a sigmoid for CTR.
diagram:
flowchart TD W["Wide: 稀疏人工交叉特征
线性→记忆"] --> S(("相加→sigmoid")) D["Deep: 稠密 embedding
前馈网→泛化"] --> S S --> CTR["CTR 预测"]
options: Wide 和 Deep 各自独立训练两个模型,像集成学习一样线上分别打分后取平均,不共享损失也不联合优化
Wide 线性建模人工交叉做记忆,Deep 用 embedding 做泛化,相加过 sigmoid
Wide 处理图像特征、Deep 处理文本特征,两个模态各走一路、最后在输出层拼接,和记忆/泛化无关
Wide 是深层网络负责泛化未见组合,Deep 是线性模型负责记忆高频共现,两者角色正好互换
options_en: Wide and Deep are trained independently like an ensemble, scored separately online and averaged, sharing no loss and not jointly optimized.
Wide linearly models manual crosses for memorization, Deep uses embeddings for generalization, summed into a sigmoid.
Wide handles image features and Deep handles text features, each modality on its own path concatenated at the output layer, unrelated to memorization/generalization.
Wide is the deep net responsible for generalizing to unseen combos, and Deep is the linear model responsible for memorizing frequent co-occurrences — their roles are swapped.
optionExplanations: W&D 是联合训练、共享损失、输出相加,不是像集成学习那样独立训练再取平均。
对;wide 记忆高频共现、deep 泛化未见组合,联合训练相加过 sigmoid 出 CTR,正是原论文结构。
两支处理的是同一批表格特征的不同表示(稀疏交叉 vs 稠密 embedding),不是图像/文本分模态。
角色说反了:wide 是线性模型做记忆(高频共现),deep 是网络做泛化(未见组合),不能互换。
optionExplanations_en: W&D is jointly trained with a shared loss and summed outputs, not two independent models trained separately like an ensemble and averaged.
Correct — wide memorizes frequent co-occurrences, deep generalizes to unseen combos, jointly trained and summed into a sigmoid for CTR, the original design.
Both branches process representations of the same tabular features (sparse crosses vs dense embeddings), not separate image/text modalities.
The roles are swapped: wide is the linear memorizer (frequent co-occurrences), deep is the generalizing net (unseen combos); they can't be exchanged.

termDefinitions.meaning: Google 2016 排序模型,线性 wide(记忆)与深度 deep(泛化)联合训练。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Wide & Deep (W&D) is Google's 2016 ranking model jointly training a linear wide (memorization) and deep (generalization) part.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率,曝光被点击的概率,排序模型常见的预测目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR (Click-Through Rate) is the probability an impression is clicked, a common ranking prediction target.

termDefinitions.meaning: 利用历史高频共现(如已装×曝光)直接记住有效交叉,wide 部分负责。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Memorization exploits frequent historical co-occurrences to directly capture effective crosses, handled by the wide part.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对没见过的特征组合也能给出合理预测,deep 部分靠稠密 embedding 负责。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Generalization gives sensible predictions for unseen feature combinations, handled by the deep part via dense embeddings.

scenario: 解释 Wide & Deep 为什么两条支路都要,而不是只留一条。
scenario_en: Explaining why Wide & Deep needs both branches rather than just one.
q: wide 的「记忆」和 deep 的「泛化」在能力上如何互补？
q_en: How do wide's memorization and deep's generalization complement each other?
why: wide 靠人工交叉记住高频强共现(deep 会平滑掉),deep 靠稠密 embedding 泛化到未见组合。单用 wide 不会泛化、单用 deep 漏掉尖锐规则,合起来才互补、强于任一支。
why_en: Wide memorizes sharp high-frequency co-occurrences that deep would smooth over, while deep generalizes to sparse unseen combos, so together they beat either alone.
tradeoff: wide 记忆(高频共现精准但不泛化) vs deep 泛化(覆盖未见组合但平滑掉尖锐规则)
options: 两支能力完全重叠,留一支即可,另一支纯属冗余没有增益
wide 记忆高频共现(deep 会平滑掉)、deep 泛化未见组合,互补优于任一支
wide 负责泛化未见组合、deep 负责记忆高频共现,两者角色和实际正好相反
两支都只做记忆,区别仅在于 wide 用 CPU、deep 用 GPU,能力上没有分工
options_en: The two branches fully overlap; keep one, the other is pure redundancy with no gain.
Wide memorizes high-frequency co-occurrences that deep smooths away, deep generalizes to unseen combos.
Wide generalizes to unseen combos and deep memorizes high-frequency co-occurrences — roles exactly opposite to reality.
Both branches only memorize; the sole difference is wide uses CPU and deep uses GPU, with no capability split.
optionExplanations: 两支能力不重叠:一个记忆尖锐规则、一个泛化新组合,去掉任一支都掉能力。
对;记忆与泛化是互补的两种能力,合起来才既抓高频又覆盖长尾,优于单支。
角色说反了:wide 记忆、deep 泛化,不能互换。
分工不是硬件差异,而是记忆 vs 泛化两种建模能力的差异。
optionExplanations_en: The branches don't overlap: one memorizes sharp rules, the other generalizes new combos; dropping either loses capability.
Correct — memorization and generalization are complementary, together capturing both frequent and long-tail patterns, beating either alone.
Roles reversed: wide memorizes, deep generalizes; they can't be swapped.
The split isn't hardware but two modeling capabilities, memorization vs generalization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把两个特征组合成新特征(如已装 app×曝光 app),让线性模型捕捉共现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature cross combines two features (e.g. installed-app × impression-app) so a linear model can capture co-occurrence.

scenario: 排序模型现在是纯逻辑回归(LR),既有大量稀疏类别特征,又新增了不少稠密 embedding 特征,想升级但不想丢掉线性模型的记忆力。
scenario_en: The ranker is plain logistic regression with lots of sparse categoricals plus new dense embeddings, and you want to upgrade without losing linear memorization.
q: 从纯 LR 往上升级,最自然的下一步是什么？
q_en: Escalating from plain LR, what's the most natural next step?
why: 纯 LR 大致等于 W&D 的 wide 支路。既然同时有稀疏类别+稠密 embedding,自然升级就是加一条 deep 支路变 Wide & Deep:保住记忆力,再补未见组合的泛化。
why_en: Plain LR is roughly W&D's wide branch, so adding a deep branch to form Wide & Deep keeps the memorization and adds generalization for the new dense embeddings.
tradeoff: 升级为 W&D(保留 LR 记忆+加 deep 泛化,平滑过渡) vs 直接上更复杂结构(收益不确定、丢失渐进性)
options: 把 LR 直接换成一个纯深度前馈网,把稀疏类别也全部走 embedding,彻底丢掉线性支路
在 LR(≈wide 支路)上加一条 deep 支路,变成 Wide & Deep 补上泛化
退回到 GBDT,放弃新增的稠密 embedding 特征,只用手工交叉的树模型继续做排序
保持纯 LR 架构不变,只把新增的稠密 embedding 特征离散化后塞进稀疏交叉里
options_en: Replace LR outright with a pure deep feed-forward net, routing sparse categoricals through embeddings too, dropping the linear branch entirely.
Add a deep branch on top of LR (≈ the wide branch), forming Wide & Deep to add generalization.
Revert to GBDT, abandon the newly added dense embedding features, and keep ranking with a hand-crossed tree model only.
Keep the plain LR architecture but discretize the new dense embedding features and stuff them into sparse crosses instead.
whenOtherWins: 若手工特征交叉的维护成本已成主要痛点、想彻底自动化交叉,则该跳过 W&D 直接上 DCN(自动交叉)。
whenOtherWins_en: If manual feature-cross maintenance is the main pain and you want crosses fully automated, skip W&D and go straight to DCN.
optionExplanations: 把稀疏类别硬塞进 embedding 会丢掉 LR 的尖锐记忆力,对高频强共现反而变差,不是最平滑的升级。
对;LR≈wide,加 deep 支路即 W&D,保留记忆又补泛化,是最自然的下一步。
退回 GBDT 等于放弃刚拿到手的稠密 embedding 特征和泛化能力,和「升级」方向相反。
把稠密 embedding 硬离散化再塞进线性交叉,丢失了 embedding 本该带来的连续泛化能力,本质还是纯 LR,没有真正升级。
optionExplanations_en: Forcing sparse categoricals through embeddings drops LR's sharp memorization and does worse on frequent strong co-occurrences, not the smoothest upgrade.
Correct — LR ≈ wide, so adding a deep branch is W&D, keeping memorization and adding generalization, the natural next step.
Reverting to GBDT abandons the newly gained dense embedding features and their generalization power, opposite to upgrading.
Discretizing the dense embeddings and stuffing them into linear crosses throws away the continuous generalization embeddings were supposed to add — it's still plain LR underneath, not a real upgrade.

termDefinitions.term: sparse categorical feature / 稀疏类别特征
termDefinitions.meaning: 取值离散且高基数的特征(如 app ID),线性 wide 支路擅长记忆其交叉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sparse categorical feature is a high-cardinality discrete feature (e.g. app ID) whose crosses the wide branch memorizes well.

scenario: W&D 的 wide 支路要人工设计特征交叉,团队想让交叉自动化。
scenario_en: W&D's wide branch needs hand-designed feature crosses, and the team wants crosses automated.
q: DCN(Deep & Cross Network)相对 W&D 的关键改进是什么？
q_en: What is DCN's (Deep & Cross Network) key improvement over W&D?
why: DCN 用 cross-network 每层做显式特征交叉,每加一层多一阶交互,L 层自动捕捉 (L+1) 阶交叉,消除 wide 支路的人工交叉。deep 支路并行,cross+deep 拼接进最终预测层。
why_en: DCN's cross-network does explicit feature crossing per layer so L layers automatically capture up to (L+1)-order interactions, eliminating W&D's manual feature crossing.
options: DCN 把 deep 支路删掉,只保留一个更大的线性层来手工枚举所有可能的特征交叉
DCN 用 cross-network 每层显式自动交叉(L 层→(L+1)阶),消除人工交叉
DCN 只是把 W&D 换了个名字,内部结构和训练方式完全一样,没有任何机制改进
DCN 靠更大的 embedding 维度来隐式交叉,完全不引入任何专门的 cross 层结构
options_en: DCN removes the deep branch and keeps one larger linear layer that hand-enumerates all possible crosses.
DCN cross-network does explicit automatic crossing per layer (L layers → (L+1)-order), removing manual crosses.
DCN is just W&D renamed; the internal structure and training are identical with no mechanism change.
DCN relies on a larger embedding dimension for implicit crossing and introduces no dedicated cross-layer structure.
optionExplanations: DCN 保留 deep 支路;它替换的是 wide 的人工交叉,不是靠更大线性层手工枚举。
对;cross-network 逐层自动升阶交叉,把人工特征交叉自动化,这正是 DCN 的核心改进。
DCN 有实质机制改进(cross-network 自动交叉),不是改名。
更大 embedding 不等于显式交叉;DCN 的关键正是专门的 cross 层显式建交互。
optionExplanations_en: DCN keeps the deep branch; it replaces wide's manual crosses, not via a larger hand-enumerating linear layer.
Correct — the cross-network automatically raises interaction order per layer, automating manual crosses, DCN's core improvement.
DCN has a real mechanism change (automatic crossing), not a rename.
A bigger embedding isn't explicit crossing; DCN's point is a dedicated cross layer that models interactions explicitly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 W&D 上用 cross-network 自动做显式特征交叉,消除人工交叉工程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DCN (Deep & Cross Network) uses a cross-network for automatic explicit feature crossing, removing manual cross engineering.

termDefinitions.meaning: 逐层做显式特征交叉的网络,每层多一阶交互,L 层达 (L+1) 阶。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-network performs explicit feature crossing per layer, each adding one interaction order, reaching (L+1)-order after L layers.

scenario: DCN 的 cross 层数要定几层:每层成本 ∝ 层数 × 输入维度,高维稀疏输入下会成瓶颈。
scenario_en: Choosing DCN's cross-layer count: each layer costs ∝ #layers × input dim, and high-dim sparse inputs can bottleneck.
q: DCN 的 cross 层数为什么常取 2-3 层这个甜点区？
q_en: Why is DCN's cross-layer count commonly kept at the 2-3 sweet spot?
why: L 层 cross 能自动捕捉到 (L+1) 阶交互,前几阶交互带来的收益最大;但 cross 成本 ∝ 层数 × 输入维度,高维稀疏输入下层数一多就成算力瓶颈。2-3 层在「够高阶」与「不炸算力」之间取平衡,是常用甜点区。
why_en: L layers capture (L+1)-order interactions with the biggest gains from the first few orders, while cost scales with #layers × input dim, so 2-3 layers balance order against compute.
options: 因为 cross 层只能取奇数,2-3 层是唯一合法的层数配置
因为高阶交互收益递减,而 cross 成本∝层数×输入维度,2-3 层是平衡点
因为 2-3 层能把所有 (L+1) 阶以上的无穷阶交互一次性全部精确建出来
因为层数越多精度一定越高,取 2-3 层纯粹是因为训练框架的上限限制
options_en: Because cross layers must be odd, so 2-3 is the only legal configuration.
Because high-order gains diminish while cost scales with layers × input dim, so 2-3 is the balance point.
Because 2-3 layers exactly build all infinite-order interactions beyond (L+1) at once.
Because more layers always mean higher accuracy, and 2-3 is purely a training-framework upper limit.
optionExplanations: 层数没有奇偶限制;2-3 是收益与成本的平衡点,不是唯一合法值。
对;前几阶交互收益最大、再往上成本随维度飙升,2-3 层是够用又不炸算力的甜点区。
L 层只到 (L+1) 阶,不可能一次建出无穷阶交互,这句本身不成立。
层数越多不必然越准,还会增本增噪;取 2-3 层是收益/成本权衡而非框架上限。
optionExplanations_en: There's no odd/even rule; 2-3 is a gain-vs-cost balance, not the only legal value.
Correct — the first few orders give the most gain while cost climbs with dimension, so 2-3 layers is the enough-yet-affordable sweet spot.
L layers reach only (L+1)-order, so building infinite-order at once is false.
More layers don't guarantee accuracy and add cost and noise; 2-3 is a gain/cost tradeoff, not a framework cap.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同时参与一次特征交叉的原始特征个数;DCN 的 L 层达到 (L+1) 阶。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Interaction order is how many raw features join one cross; DCN's L layers reach (L+1)-order.

scenario: DCN-v2(2021)相对初代 DCN 在 cross 层的权重上做了改动。
scenario_en: DCN-v2 (2021) changes the weight in the cross layer relative to the original DCN.
q: DCN-v2 相比初代 DCN 的主要改动与代价是什么？
q_en: What does DCN-v2 change from the original DCN, and at what cost?
why: DCN-v2 把 cross 层里的向量权重 w_l 换成矩阵 W_l,让每层能表达更丰富的交叉,精度可比甚至优于 W&D,还免去人工交叉;代价是参数量更多、算力更大。它把加新特征的迭代从「天」缩短到「小时」。
why_en: DCN-v2 replaces the cross layer's vector weight w_l with a matrix W_l for richer crosses, matching or beating W&D without manual crosses, at the cost of more parameters.
tradeoff: DCN-v2 矩阵权重 W_l(交叉更丰富、精度更高) vs 初代向量权重 w_l(参数更少、表达力较弱)
options: DCN-v2 把 cross 层删掉只留 deep 支路,靠更深的前馈网代替显式交叉
DCN-v2 把 cross 层向量权重 w_l 换成矩阵 W_l,交叉更丰富但参数更多
DCN-v2 重新引入了人工特征交叉,放弃了初代的自动交叉能力
DCN-v2 只是把初代模型量化压缩,不改变 cross 层结构,纯粹为了省显存
options_en: DCN-v2 removes the cross layer, keeping only the deep branch, replacing explicit crosses with a deeper feed-forward net.
DCN-v2 swaps the cross layer vector weight w_l for a matrix W_l: richer crosses, more parameters.
DCN-v2 reintroduces manual feature crosses, abandoning the original's automatic crossing.
DCN-v2 just quantizes and compresses the original without changing the cross layer, purely to save VRAM.
optionExplanations: DCN-v2 保留并增强 cross 层,不是删掉它换更深 deep。
对;向量权重→矩阵权重是 v2 的核心改动,换来更丰富交叉与更高精度,代价是参数更多。
v2 恰恰继续自动交叉,并未回到人工交叉。
v2 是结构增强(矩阵权重)而非单纯量化压缩。
optionExplanations_en: DCN-v2 keeps and strengthens the cross layer, not removes it for a deeper deep branch.
Correct — vector-to-matrix weight is v2's core change, buying richer crosses and higher accuracy at more parameters.
v2 continues automatic crossing and doesn't return to manual crosses.
v2 is a structural upgrade (matrix weight), not mere quantization/compression.

termDefinitions.meaning: 2021 版 DCN,cross 层用矩阵权重 W_l 替代向量 w_l,交叉更丰富。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DCN-v2 (2021) replaces the cross layer's vector weight with a matrix W_l for richer feature crosses.

scenario: 排序团队每次加一个新特征,都要人工设计它和别的特征怎么交叉,迭代一次要好几天,想提速。
scenario_en: Every new feature requires hand-designing its crosses, taking days per iteration, and the team wants to speed up.
q: 为了摆脱人工特征交叉、加快迭代,该在 W&D 和 DCN 之间选谁？
q_en: To drop manual feature crossing and iterate faster, choose W&D or DCN?
why: DCN 更合适:cross-network 自动做显式交叉,不用人工设计每个特征怎么交叉,把加新特征的迭代从「天」压到「小时」,精度还可比/优于 W&D。W&D 的 wide 支路恰恰要人工交叉,正是团队想摆脱的负担。
why_en: DCN fits: its cross-network automates explicit crossing so you skip hand-designing crosses, cutting feature-add iteration from days to hours while matching or beating W&D.
tradeoff: DCN(自动交叉、迭代小时级、算力中等) vs W&D(人工交叉、迭代天级、但结构更简单成熟)
options: 选 W&D,因为人工按业务经验设计的交叉一定比自动交叉更准,多花几天也值得
选 DCN:cross-network 自动做显式交叉,迭代从天缩到小时
两者都不选,退回纯 LR,靠人工精简特征来减少要交叉的组合数,绕开自动化
选谁都行,W&D 和 DCN 在是否需要人工设计交叉这一点上其实没有实质区别
options_en: Choose W&D because crosses hand-designed from business experience are always more accurate than automatic ones, worth the extra days.
Choose DCN: the cross-network automates explicit crossing and cuts iteration from days to hours.
Choose neither; revert to plain LR and manually trim features to shrink the combinations that need crossing, sidestepping automation.
Either is fine — W&D and DCN don't actually differ substantively on whether manual cross design is needed.
whenOtherWins: 若少数几个关键交叉靠领域知识人工设计能显著提点、且特征集稳定不常变,W&D 的人工交叉反而更可控。
whenOtherWins_en: If a few key crosses hand-designed from domain knowledge boost metrics a lot and the feature set is stable, W&D's manual crosses can be more controllable.
optionExplanations: 人工交叉不必然更准,即使是业务经验驱动的交叉,DCN 自动交叉精度也可比/更优,还省掉几天迭代成本。
对;DCN 自动化交叉直击「人工设计慢」的痛点,迭代提速且精度不降,是对症之选。
退回纯 LR 靠人工精简特征依然要人工判断留哪些交叉,是砍能力换简单,解决不了「想保留交叉但要自动化」的诉求。
两者关键区别正是在此:W&D 需人工设计交叉,DCN 自动交叉,不能说没有实质区别。
optionExplanations_en: Manual crosses aren't necessarily more accurate — even business-experience-driven crosses are matched/beaten by DCN's automatic crosses, which also save days of iteration.
Correct — DCN's automation targets the 'manual design is slow' pain, speeding iteration without losing accuracy.
Reverting to LR and manually trimming features still requires manually judging which crosses to keep — trading capability for simplicity, and doesn't meet the 'keep crosses but automate' need.
This is exactly their key difference: W&D needs hand-designed crosses, DCN automates them, so they do differ substantively.

termDefinitions.term: feature engineering burden / 特征工程负担
termDefinitions.meaning: 人工设计与维护特征交叉的成本;DCN 自动化交叉以降低它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Feature-engineering burden is the cost of hand-designing and maintaining crosses, which DCN reduces via automatic crossing.

scenario: 把两塔、Wide & Deep、DCN 放在一张决策矩阵上,准备在面试里说清各自定位。
scenario_en: Placing two-tower, Wide & Deep, and DCN on one decision matrix to state each one's role in an interview.
q: 两塔、W&D、DCN 分别处在级联的哪一阶段、各自的特征工程负担如何？
q_en: Which cascade stage do two-tower, W&D, and DCN serve, and what's each one's feature-engineering burden?
why: 两塔用于检索(用户/物品编码器+ANN,交互弱但快,sub-10ms);W&D 用于排序(记忆强,但要人工交叉,FE 负担高);DCN 用于排序(自动交叉,FE 负担低,算力中等)。定位不同:一个负责收窄规模,两个负责精打分。
why_en: Two-tower serves retrieval (encoders + ANN, fast, weak interaction), while W&D and DCN serve ranking, with W&D carrying high manual-cross burden and DCN automating crosses.
tradeoff: 两塔(检索、快、交互弱) vs W&D(排序、记忆强、人工交叉贵) vs DCN(排序、自动交叉、算力中等)
options: 三者都用于检索阶段,谁也不做排序,靠堆三个检索模型串联来提升召回
两塔=检索(快、交互弱);W&D、DCN=排序(前者人工交叉,后者自动)
三者都是排序模型,没有一个能做检索,检索只能靠关键词匹配
两塔用于排序,W&D 和 DCN 用于检索,三者的阶段定位正好和实际相反
options_en: All three serve retrieval, none does ranking, chaining three retrieval models to boost recall.
Two-tower = retrieval (fast, weak interaction); W&D and DCN = ranking, with manual vs automatic crossing.
All three are rankers, none can do retrieval, and retrieval must rely on keyword matching.
Two-tower does ranking while W&D and DCN do retrieval — the stage roles are exactly reversed.
optionExplanations: 两塔才用于检索,W&D/DCN 是排序;三者不是同阶段堆叠,而是级联分工。
对;两塔收窄规模、W&D/DCN 精打分,FE 负担 W&D 高、DCN 低,这就是三者定位。
两塔正是可做检索的架构,说三者都不能检索与事实不符。
阶段说反了:两塔检索、W&D/DCN 排序,不能互换。
optionExplanations_en: Only two-tower serves retrieval while W&D/DCN rank; they aren't stacked at one stage but split across the cascade.
Correct — two-tower narrows scale, W&D/DCN score precisely, with W&D high and DCN low on FE burden, their exact roles.
Two-tower is precisely the retrieval-capable architecture, so 'none can retrieve' is false.
Stages reversed: two-tower retrieves, W&D/DCN rank; they can't be swapped.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工设计特征/交叉的工作量:W&D 高、DCN 低、两塔中等。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Feature-engineering (FE) burden is the manual work of designing features/crosses: high for W&D, low for DCN, moderate for two-tower.

termDefinitions.meaning: 深度神经网络,W&D 的 deep 支路与 DCN 的并行支路都是它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNN (Deep Neural Network) is the deep branch in W&D and the parallel branch in DCN.

q: 把两塔检索的线上服务流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the online serving flow of two-tower retrieval:
steps: 线上收到请求,只跑用户塔算出用户向量
离线用物品塔把全部物品预计算成向量
拿用户向量到 ANN 索引里做近邻检索,返回 top-K 候选
把物品向量灌进 ANN 索引(FAISS/ScaNN)
why: 离线两步先行:物品塔预算物品向量 → 灌进 ANN 索引;线上两步随请求:只跑用户塔得用户向量 → ANN 近邻检索 top-K。把重活(十亿物品编码)放离线、线上只算一个用户向量,是 sub-10ms 的关键。
why_en: Offline first precompute item vectors then index them in ANN; online run only the user tower then do an ANN top-K lookup, keeping the heavy item encoding offline.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["离线:物品塔预算物品向量"] --> B["灌进 ANN 索引"]
  B --> C["线上:用户塔算用户向量"]
  C --> D["ANN 近邻检索 top-K"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 对物品向量建的索引(FAISS/ScaNN),支持毫秒级 top-K 相似检索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ANN index (FAISS/ScaNN) over item vectors supports millisecond top-K similarity retrieval.

q: 填空:两塔检索的部署要点。
q_en: Fill in the two-tower retrieval deployment essentials.
text: 物品 embedding 在{{离线}}预计算并灌进 {{ANN}} 索引(FAISS/ScaNN);线上只跑{{用户塔}},用它的向量做近邻检索,top-K 在 {{sub-10ms}} 内返回。
text_en: Item embeddings are precomputed {{offline}} and indexed in an {{ANN}} system (FAISS/ScaNN); online only the {{user tower}} runs, and its vector retrieves top-K within {{sub-10ms}}.
why: 记住「物品离线 + 用户在线 + ANN 检索」这条部署主线:重活放离线固化,线上只算一个向量再近邻查,才能在 sub-10ms 里从十亿物品取回候选。
why_en: Remember offline items + online user + ANN lookup: freeze the heavy work offline so online computes one vector then a nearest-neighbor query within sub-10ms.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 ANN 索引里取与用户向量最相似的 K 个物品作为候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Top-K retrieval returns the K items most similar to the user vector from the ANN index as candidates.

scenario: 两塔里物品有十亿量级,每次用户请求都要在 sub-200ms 端到端内返回候选。
scenario_en: A two-tower with a billion items must return candidates within a sub-200ms end-to-end budget per request.
q: 为什么两塔一定要把物品 embedding 离线预计算,而不是请求时现算？
q_en: Why must a two-tower precompute item embeddings offline rather than at query time?
why: 请求时给十亿物品逐个跑物品塔算 embedding,计算量远超 sub-200ms 预算,直接顶破延迟约束。离线把物品向量算好灌进 ANN,线上只算一个用户向量再近邻检索,才能满足延迟。这正是两塔解耦设计的目的。
why_en: Computing embeddings for a billion items at query time far exceeds the latency budget, so items are precomputed offline into ANN while online only the user vector is computed.
tradeoff: 离线预算物品向量(满足延迟、但物品更新有滞后) vs 请求时现算(最新但十亿级违反延迟约束)
options: 因为请求时逐个算十亿物品 embedding 远超延迟预算,离线+ANN 才够快
因为物品 embedding 离线算出来精度更高、更稳定,和线上延迟预算没关系
因为物品塔太大装不进线上服务器内存,只能在离线机器上跑一次
因为请求时算 embedding 会泄露用户隐私,离线算是出于合规要求
options_en: Because computing a billion item embeddings at query time blows the latency budget; offline + ANN is fast enough.
Because offline item embeddings are more accurate and stable, unrelated to the online latency budget.
Because the item tower is too large to fit in online server memory and can only run once on offline machines.
Because computing embeddings at query time leaks user privacy, so offline is a compliance requirement.
whenOtherWins: 若物品只有几千条且频繁变化,请求时现算物品向量也能满足延迟,离线预算+ANN 的收益就不明显了。
whenOtherWins_en: If there are only a few thousand items that change often, computing item vectors at query time can meet latency and offline+ANN buys little.
optionExplanations: 对;十亿物品请求时逐个前向必然超预算,离线固化+ANN 才把延迟压回 sub-200ms 内。
离线算不必更准;真正原因是延迟约束,不是精度。
内存不是根因;即便装得下,逐个前向十亿物品的时间也过不了预算。
隐私不是这里的原因;物品 embedding 与用户隐私无关,预算约束才是主因。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — forward-passing a billion items per request must exceed budget; freezing offline + ANN brings latency back within sub-200ms.
Offline isn't inherently more accurate; the real reason is the latency constraint, not accuracy.
Memory isn't the cause; even if it fit, forward-passing a billion items per request exceeds the budget.
Privacy isn't the reason; item embeddings don't involve user privacy — the budget constraint is.

termDefinitions.meaning: 离线提前算好物品向量并索引,避免请求时重复对海量物品做前向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precompute means computing and indexing item vectors offline to avoid re-running forward passes over many items per request.

scenario: 要给级联的两个阶段各选模型:一个面对十亿量级要极快,一个面对数百候选要尽量准。
scenario_en: Choosing a model for each cascade stage: one faces billions and must be very fast, one faces hundreds and must be accurate.
q: 检索阶段和排序阶段对模型的要求为什么正好相反？
q_en: Why are the model requirements for retrieval and ranking essentially opposite?
why: 检索面对十亿量级,必须轻量可预计算(两塔+ANN),牺牲交互建模换速度;排序只剩数百候选,可以上表达力强、算交互的重模型(W&D/DCN)换精度。同一个模型无法同时满足两端,所以按阶段分工选不同架构。
why_en: Retrieval faces billions and must be light and precomputable, trading interaction for speed, while ranking faces hundreds and can afford an expressive interaction-modeling model for accuracy.
tradeoff: 检索(轻量可预计算、交互弱、快) vs 排序(重、交互强、准,但只处理少量候选)
options: 因为检索和排序其实要求一样,都追求又快又准,用同一个模型跑两遍就行
检索面对十亿要轻量可预计算,排序只剩数百可上重模型算交互
因为检索要最准、排序要最快,所以检索用重模型、排序用轻模型
因为检索和排序的差别只是数据库不同,和模型架构选择完全无关
options_en: Because retrieval and ranking actually have the same requirements — both want fast and accurate — so one model run twice suffices.
Retrieval faces billions and must stay light and precomputable; ranking faces hundreds and can model interaction.
Because retrieval wants maximum accuracy and ranking wants maximum speed, so retrieval uses the heavy model and ranking the light one.
Because the difference is only the database used, unrelated to model architecture choice.
whenOtherWins: 若候选集本就很小(几千条),检索这一层几乎可省,直接用一个排序重模型给全部候选打分也能满足延迟。
whenOtherWins_en: If the candidate set is small (a few thousand), the retrieval layer is nearly unneeded and one heavy ranker over all candidates can meet latency.
optionExplanations: 两端要求相反:一个求快、一个求准,同一模型很难同时满足,所以才分阶段。
对;规模决定了检索必须轻、排序才付得起重,这正是级联按阶段选不同架构的原因。
分反了:检索面对十亿必须最快(轻模型),排序候选少才用重模型求准。
差别不在数据库而在规模/延迟对模型的要求,直接决定架构选择。
optionExplanations_en: The ends are opposite: one wants speed, one wants accuracy, and one model can't do both — hence two stages.
Correct — scale dictates retrieval be light and ranking afford heavy, the reason the cascade picks different architectures per stage.
Reversed: retrieval faces billions and must be fastest (light), ranking with few candidates uses the heavy model for accuracy.
The difference is scale/latency demands on the model, not the database, and it drives architecture choice.

termDefinitions.term: cascade division of labor / 级联分工
termDefinitions.meaning: 检索轻量收窄规模、排序重模型精打分,两阶段各司其职。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cascade division of labor has light retrieval narrow the scale and a heavy ranker score precisely, each stage playing its role.

scenario: 两塔把用户和物品分开编码,直到最后才用点积相遇。
scenario_en: A two-tower encodes user and item separately, meeting only at a final dot product.
q: 两塔为了速度牺牲了什么,这个代价怎么补？
q_en: What does two-tower sacrifice for speed, and how is that cost mitigated?
why: 两塔用户与物品直到末端点积才相遇,中间无法建模细粒度的用户-物品特征交互,交互建模弱——这是它换取「可预计算+ANN 快速检索」付出的代价。补法:让下游的排序阶段(W&D/DCN,或蒸自 cross-encoder)把交互建模补回来。
why_en: Two-tower can't model fine-grained user-item interaction since they meet only at the final dot product, trading interaction for precomputable speed, mitigated by the downstream ranker.
tradeoff: 两塔(可预计算、快检索) vs 牺牲用户-物品细粒度交互建模(靠下游排序补回)
options: 牺牲了训练速度,补法是买更多 GPU 让两塔训得更快
牺牲细粒度用户-物品交互(末端才点积),靠下游排序补回来
牺牲了 embedding 维度,补法是把向量维度扩到上万维
两塔没有牺牲任何东西,它在速度和交互建模上都是最优的
options_en: It sacrifices training speed; mitigate by buying more GPUs so the towers train faster.
It sacrifices fine-grained user-item interaction (they meet only at the dot product); the downstream ranker compensates.
It sacrifices embedding dimension; mitigate by expanding vectors to tens of thousands of dims.
Two-tower sacrifices nothing; it's optimal on both speed and interaction modeling.
optionExplanations: 牺牲的不是训练速度,而是推理时的交互建模;加 GPU 补不回结构上缺的交互。
对;分开编码换来了可预计算的快检索,代价是交互弱,靠下游排序阶段把交互补回来。
维度不是牺牲点;盲目扩维增本还未必补回交互,治标不治本。
两塔确有牺牲(交互建模),说它两端都最优不成立。
optionExplanations_en: It sacrifices interaction modeling at inference, not training speed; GPUs can't restore structurally missing interaction.
Correct — separate encoding buys precomputable fast retrieval at weak interaction, restored by the downstream ranker.
Dimension isn't the sacrifice; blindly expanding it adds cost without truly restoring interaction.
Two-tower does sacrifice interaction, so claiming it's optimal on both is false.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户与物品向量只在最后点积相遇,中途不交互,故交互建模弱。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Late interaction means user and item vectors meet only at a final dot product, so interaction modeling is weak.

scenario: 设计两塔时要决定每座塔喂什么特征。
scenario_en: Designing a two-tower, you decide what features feed each tower.
q: 以下哪些是两塔各自常见的输入特征?(多选)
q_en: Which are common inputs to each two-tower? (multiple)
why: 用户塔吃用户侧信号:观看历史、人口属性、上下文(如一天中的时段);物品塔吃物品侧信号:物品 ID、标题 embedding、类别、热度。两侧各自编码成同维向量,不能把物品的原始视频码率这类无语义的传输参数当建模特征。
why_en: The user tower takes watch history, demographics, and context, while the item tower takes item ID, title embedding, category, and popularity, each encoded into same-dim vectors.
options: 用户塔:观看历史、人口属性、上下文(如时段)
物品塔:物品 ID、标题 embedding、类别、热度
两塔都需要:各自把特征编码成同维稠密向量
物品塔:视频的原始网络传输码率与 CDN 节点 IP
options_en: User tower: watch history, demographics, context (e.g. time of day).
Item tower: item ID, title embedding, category, popularity.
Both towers: each encodes features into a same-dimension dense vector.
Item tower: the video's raw network bitrate and CDN node IP.
optionExplanations: 对;用户侧的历史/人口/上下文是刻画用户口味的核心信号。
对;物品侧的 ID/标题/类别/热度共同刻画物品,编码成物品向量。
对;两塔输出必须同维,才能做点积/余弦相似度检索。
错;码率和 CDN IP 是传输/分发参数,无推荐语义,不该当建模特征。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — user-side history/demographics/context are core signals of user taste.
Correct — item-side ID/title/category/popularity together characterize the item as a vector.
Correct — both towers must output the same dimension to do dot-product/cosine similarity.
Wrong — bitrate and CDN IP are delivery parameters with no rec semantics and shouldn't be modeling features.

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求时的情境信号(时段、设备等),喂进用户塔刻画当下场景。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Context features are request-time situational signals (time of day, device) fed to the user tower to capture the moment.

scenario: 面试白板上画两塔时,除了画两座塔和点积,还需要标注哪些信息才算讲清楚。
scenario_en: Sketching two-tower on the whiteboard, beyond the towers and dot product, what must you annotate to be clear?
q: 画两塔检索图时,最该标注的是哪一项？
q_en: When sketching two-tower retrieval, what is most important to annotate?
why: 关键是标出「离线 vs 在线」的边界:物品索引在 FAISS/ScaNN 里离线预算,用户塔在线跑,并标上 sub-10ms 延迟。这条边界解释了两塔为何能在十亿级做到低延迟,是面试官最想看到的成本/延迟意识,而不是画得好不好看。
why_en: Mark the offline vs online boundary — item index in FAISS/ScaNN offline, user tower online — and annotate the sub-10ms latency, which explains how two-tower scales.
tradeoff: 标注离线/在线边界+延迟(体现规模化推理) vs 只画结构框(看不出为何能低延迟)
options: 把每座塔画成几层、每层多少神经元,精确标注网络深度和宽度
标出离线物品索引(FAISS/ScaNN)与在线用户塔的边界
标注训练用的 GPU 型号和 batch size,让面试官知道算力配置
把用户和物品的全部原始特征名一个不漏地写满整块白板
options_en: Draw each tower's layer count and neurons per layer, annotating exact depth and width.
Mark the boundary between the offline item index (FAISS/ScaNN) and the online user tower.
Annotate the training GPU model and batch size so the interviewer knows the compute setup.
Write out every raw feature name for user and item, missing none, filling the whole board.
whenOtherWins: 若讨论已聚焦到「模型容量是否够」,那时标注塔的深度/宽度才有意义;但讲检索为何低延迟时,边界+延迟最关键。
whenOtherWins_en: If the discussion has narrowed to model capacity, annotating depth/width matters then; but to explain low-latency retrieval, the boundary and latency come first.
optionExplanations: 层数神经元数是次要实现细节,标了也解释不了两塔为何能规模化低延迟。
对;离线/在线边界 + 延迟标注直接讲清两塔的规模化推理逻辑,是面试最想看到的。
GPU 型号与 batch size 是训练配置,与「为何在线检索快」无关。
堆满原始特征名信息过载,反而盖住了边界这个关键点。
optionExplanations_en: Layer/neuron counts are minor implementation details and don't explain why two-tower scales at low latency.
Correct — the offline/online boundary plus latency directly explains two-tower's scalable inference, what interviewers most want.
GPU model and batch size are training config, unrelated to why online retrieval is fast.
Cramming raw feature names overloads the board and hides the key boundary point.

termDefinitions.term: offline/online boundary / 离线在线边界
termDefinitions.meaning: 图上区分哪部分离线预算(物品索引)哪部分在线实时(用户塔)的分界。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The offline/online boundary marks which parts are precomputed offline (item index) vs run live online (user tower).

q: 填空:DCN cross 层的机制与阶数关系。
q_en: Fill in DCN's cross-layer mechanism and order relation.
text: DCN 的 cross 层公式 x_{l+1} = x_0·x_l^T·w_l + b_l + x_l,每层多加一{{阶}}交互;叠 L 层后自动捕捉到 {{(L+1)}} 阶交叉;实践常取 {{2-3}} 层,因成本∝层数×输入维度。
text_en: DCN's cross layer x_{l+1} = x_0·x_l^T·w_l + b_l + x_l adds one interaction {{order}} per layer; after L layers it captures {{(L+1)}}-order crosses; practice uses {{2-3}} layers since cost scales with #layers × input dim.
why: 记住 cross 层「每层+1 阶、L 层达 (L+1) 阶、成本随层数×维度」这条关系:它解释了为何 2-3 层是甜点区,也解释了 DCN 如何自动替代人工交叉。
why_en: Remember each cross layer adds one order, L layers reach (L+1)-order, and cost scales with layers × dim, explaining the 2-3-layer sweet spot.

termDefinitions.meaning: cross 公式里的 +x_l,把上一层输出加回,稳定深层训练。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The residual term (+x_l) in the cross formula adds back the previous layer's output to stabilize deep training.

scenario: DCN 排序模型的输入是高维稀疏特征拼接后的向量,团队发现加 cross 层后延迟明显上升。
scenario_en: A DCN ranker's input is a high-dim sparse concatenated vector, and adding cross layers noticeably raises latency.
q: cross 层的计算成本大致随什么增长,这对高维稀疏输入意味着什么？
q_en: What does cross-layer cost scale with, and what does that mean for high-dim sparse inputs?
why: cross 成本大致 ∝ 层数 × 输入维度。高维稀疏输入拼接后维度很大,层数一多计算量线性放大,成为延迟瓶颈。设计含义:控制 cross 层数(常 2-3 层),必要时先降维,别让 cross 层把排序延迟预算吃光。
why_en: Cross cost scales roughly with #layers × input dim, so high-dim sparse inputs make layers bottleneck latency, meaning cap cross layers (often 2-3) and reduce dimension if needed.
options: cross 成本∝层数×输入维度;高维稀疏下层数一多就成延迟瓶颈
cross 成本与输入维度无关,只由 batch size 决定,和高维稀疏没关系
cross 成本随层数指数爆炸,所以哪怕 2 层也无法上线,必须彻底弃用 cross 层
cross 成本随层数下降,层数越多反而越省算力,应尽量多堆几十层
options_en: Cross cost scales with layers × input dim; with high-dim sparse inputs, more layers bottleneck latency.
Cross cost is independent of input dim and set only by batch size, unrelated to high-dim sparsity.
Cross cost explodes exponentially with layers, so even 2 layers can't ship and cross layers must be abandoned entirely.
Cross cost falls with more layers, so more layers save compute and you should stack dozens.
optionExplanations: 对;成本∝层数×维度,高维输入下多加层线性放大延迟,故限层数并考虑降维。
输入维度正是成本的关键因子,说它无关与机制矛盾。
成本随层数线性而非指数;2-3 层完全可上线,不必弃用 cross。
层数越多算力越大而非越省,堆几十层会顶破延迟预算。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — cost scales with layers × dim, so with high-dim inputs extra layers linearly inflate latency; cap layers and consider dim reduction.
Input dimension is the key cost factor, so calling it irrelevant contradicts the mechanism.
Cost scales linearly with layers, not exponentially; 2-3 layers ship fine, no need to abandon cross.
More layers cost more not less; stacking dozens would blow the latency budget.

termDefinitions.meaning: 特征拼接后的向量长度,高维稀疏输入会放大 cross 层计算量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Input dimension is the length of the concatenated feature vector; high-dim sparse inputs inflate cross-layer compute.

scenario: 排序模型(W&D/DCN)预测 CTR,面试官问训练用什么目标函数。
scenario_en: A ranker (W&D/DCN) predicts CTR, and the interviewer asks what training objective is used.
q: CTR 排序模型通常用什么目标函数,输出层是什么？
q_en: What objective and output layer does a CTR ranker typically use?
why: CTR 是二分类(点/不点),输出层用 sigmoid 压成 0-1 概率,训练用二元交叉熵(BCE)。W&D/DCN 的分支输出相加过 sigmoid,再与点击标签算 BCE。
why_en: CTR is binary (click/no-click), so the output is a sigmoid giving a 0-1 probability trained with binary cross-entropy (BCE).
options: 用均方误差回归点击次数,输出层是线性层直接输出任意实数
用二元交叉熵(BCE),输出层 sigmoid 给出点击概率
用多分类 softmax 预测点击发生在一天中的哪个小时
不需要目标函数,CTR 排序靠规则阈值直接判定点或不点
options_en: Mean-squared error regressing click counts, with a linear output emitting any real number.
Binary cross-entropy (BCE), with a sigmoid output giving the click probability.
Multiclass softmax predicting which hour of the day the click happens.
No objective needed; CTR ranking decides click/no-click by a rule threshold.
optionExplanations: CTR 是概率不是计数,MSE 回归实数不匹配二分类,也不给概率输出。
对;二分类点/不点用 sigmoid+BCE,输出可解释为点击概率,是 CTR 排序标准配置。
点击小时是另一个问题,softmax 预测时段与 CTR 二分类目标无关。
排序要学习可比的概率分数,规则阈值给不出可优化梯度也无法个性化。
optionExplanations_en: CTR is a probability not a count; MSE regressing reals mismatches binary classification and gives no probability.
Correct — click/no-click uses sigmoid + BCE, output readable as click probability, the standard CTR ranking setup.
Click hour is a different problem; softmax over hours is unrelated to the binary CTR objective.
Ranking needs comparable probability scores; a rule threshold gives no optimizable gradient and can't personalize.

termDefinitions.meaning: 二元交叉熵,二分类(如点/不点)的标准损失函数,配 sigmoid 输出。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BCE (Binary Cross-Entropy) is the standard loss for binary classification like click/no-click, paired with a sigmoid output.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把任意实数压到 0-1 的激活函数,输出可当概率解释。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sigmoid squashes any real number into 0-1, so the output reads as a probability.

q: 把排序架构从简单到自动化的演进链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the ranking-architecture evolution from simple to automated:
steps: DCN 用 cross-network 自动做显式交叉,免去人工设计
纯逻辑回归(LR),只有线性、靠人工特征
DCN-v2 把 cross 向量权重换成矩阵,交叉更丰富
Wide & Deep 加一条 deep 支路,补上泛化能力
why: 演进主线是「逐步减少人工、增强交叉表达」:LR(纯人工线性)→ W&D(加 deep 泛化,但 wide 仍人工交叉)→ DCN(自动交叉)→ DCN-v2(矩阵权重更丰富交叉)。每一步要么补能力、要么自动化,迭代成本从天降到小时。
why_en: The line reduces manual work and enriches crosses: LR → W&D (adds deep generalization) → DCN (automates crosses) → DCN-v2 (matrix weights for richer crosses).
diagram:
flowchart LR
  LR["LR 纯线性"] --> WD["W&D +deep 泛化"]
  WD --> DCN["DCN 自动交叉"]
  DCN --> V2["DCN-v2 矩阵权重"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 排序模型从人工线性逐步走向自动交叉、更强交互表达的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Architecture evolution is the ranker's path from manual linear models toward automated crossing and richer interaction.

scenario: 有人把两塔设计成共享全部参数,并且只用随机负样本训练,结果 embedding 空间坍缩、召回骤降。
scenario_en: Someone builds a two-tower sharing all parameters and trains with only random negatives; the embedding space collapses and recall crashes.
q: 「共享全部参数 + 只用随机负样本」为什么会让两塔崩掉,怎么救？
q_en: Why does 'share all params + only random negatives' break a two-tower, and how do you fix it?
why: 两塔本该学不同表示;强行共享全部参数让两侧纠缠、区分度下降,再叠加随机负样本太易 → embedding 退化、recall 骤降。救法:两塔各自独立参数 + hard negative mining 提难度。
why_en: Sharing all parameters entangles the two towers' representations and, combined with only easy random negatives, degrades the embedding space; fix with separate params and hard-negative mining.
options: 因为可训练参数太少导致模型欠拟合,救法是把两座塔合并成一个更大的共享网络来增加容量
共享全部参数让两侧表示纠缠+随机负样本太易→recall 降;救法是独立参数
因为学习率设得太高,只要把学习率调低、再训练更久,共享参数加随机负样本就都没问题了
因为底层 ANN 索引精度不够才导致召回下降,与参数共享和负采样无关,换成精确检索即可
options_en: Because too few parameters underfit; fix by merging the towers into one larger shared network.
Sharing all parameters entangles both representations and easy random negatives drop recall; fix with separate parameters.
Because the learning rate is too high; just lower it and shared params with random negatives are fine.
Because the ANN index isn't precise enough, unrelated to param sharing or negative sampling; switch to exact search.
optionExplanations: 问题不是参数太少而是共享导致表示纠缠;合并成一个网络反而更纠缠,方向错了。
对;走完「共享+随机负太易→区分度退化→recall 降→独立参数+难负例修」整链,是标准诊断。
调学习率救不了结构性纠缠和负例太易带来的信息缺口,治标不治本。
recall 骤降可直接归因于参数共享+随机负样本,推给 ANN 精度是误诊。
optionExplanations_en: The issue isn't too few params but sharing entangling representations; merging into one net entangles more, wrong direction.
Correct — it walks the chain shared+easy-negatives → collapsed discrimination → recall drop → separate params + hard negatives, the standard diagnosis.
Tuning the learning rate can't fix structural entanglement and the information gap from easy negatives.
The recall crash traces to param sharing + random negatives; blaming ANN precision is a misdiagnosis.

termDefinitions.term: embedding space collapse / 向量空间坍缩
termDefinitions.meaning: embedding 区分度退化、样本挤成一团,导致近邻检索召回骤降。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Embedding space collapse is when vectors lose discrimination and cluster together, crashing nearest-neighbor recall.

scenario: 训练两塔时在「随机负样本」和「难负样本(hard negatives)」之间配比。
scenario_en: Balancing random negatives and hard negatives when training a two-tower.
q: 随机负样本与难负样本在训练信号上有何区别？
q_en: How do random vs hard negatives differ as training signal?
why: 随机负样本大多明显无关,信号弱,只教模型区分「远处的东西」;难负样本是相似但不相关的物品,逼模型学出细粒度边界,信号强但挖掘有成本、过难还可能训不稳。实践常两者混合:随机负给覆盖,难负给区分度。
why_en: Random negatives are mostly obviously irrelevant and weak signal, while hard negatives are similar-but-irrelevant and force a fine boundary, at higher mining cost.
tradeoff: 随机负样本(便宜、覆盖广、信号弱) vs 难负样本(信号强、区分度高、挖掘贵且可能训不稳)
options: 随机负样本信号更强,因为它覆盖面广,难负样本反而没什么用
随机负样本信号弱只分明显无关,难负样本逼出细边界但挖掘贵
两者提供的训练信号完全一样,唯一区别在于难负样本的采样过程更快一些
难负样本是指和用户强相关的正确物品,应该当正样本用
options_en: Random negatives give stronger signal via broad coverage; hard negatives are useless.
Random negatives are weak signal separating only the obvious, while hard negatives force a fine boundary at higher mining cost.
The training signal is identical; the only difference is that hard negatives sample somewhat faster.
Hard negatives are strongly-relevant correct items for the user and should be used as positives.
optionExplanations: 覆盖广不等于信号强;随机负太易,难负才提供区分细边界的强信号。
对;随机负弱信号、难负强信号但挖掘贵,这条对比决定了两者的配比策略。
两者信号不同:随机负弱、难负强,不是只差训练速度。
难负是相似但不相关的负例,不是正确物品,当正样本会污染标签。
optionExplanations_en: Broad coverage isn't strong signal; random negatives are too easy, hard negatives give the strong fine-boundary signal.
Correct — random weak, hard strong but costly to mine; this contrast sets the mixing strategy.
Their signal differs: random weak, hard strong, not merely a training-speed gap.
Hard negatives are similar-but-irrelevant negatives, not correct items; using them as positives corrupts labels.

termDefinitions.meaning: 与用户相似但实际不相关的物品,作负例逼模型学细粒度相关性边界。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hard negative is an item similar to the user yet actually irrelevant, forcing a fine relevance boundary.
